claims.text: Argo CD can deploy to an external cluster registered by a Secret in its namespace labelled argocd.argoproj.io/secret-type: cluster, with keys name, server and config (JSON, e.g. tlsClientConfig with caData, certData, keyData); an Application then names that server as destination.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs v3.1: Operator Manual > Declarative Setup > Clusters

claims.text: Argo CD's own cluster (in-cluster, https://kubernetes.default.svc) is usable without a cluster Secret; in the lab staging has none, so a cluster generator with a label selector yields no parameter set for it.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs v3.1: Declarative Setup > Clusters (in-cluster); ApplicationSet > Generators > Cluster generator (local cluster and label selectors); regions-appset.yaml lines 1-5

claims.text: An ApplicationSet holds generators and an Application template; the ApplicationSet controller, installed with Argo CD's standard install manifests, creates (and updates) one Application per parameter set the generators produce.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs v3.1: Operator Manual > ApplicationSet > Introduction, Getting Started (installed with Argo CD)

claims.text: The cluster generator yields one parameter set per cluster Secret matching selector.matchLabels, with parameters name and server; with goTemplate: true the template uses {{.name}} and {{.server}}.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs v3.1: ApplicationSet > Generators > Cluster Generator; Go Template

claims.text: Deleting an ApplicationSet deletes the Applications it created (owner references), and by default (preserveResourcesOnDeletion false) those Applications carry the resources finalizer, so the resources they deployed are deleted too.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs v3.1: ApplicationSet > Application Pruning & Resource Deletion; applicationset.sh comment lines 122-125

claims.text: regions-appset.yaml @ stage-4 lines 13-37: cluster generator selecting donhang.lab/region: "true" (14-17); template name echo-{{.name}} (24), destination server {{.server}} (32); repoURL, targetRevision main, path platform/regions fixed; automated sync with selfHeal and prune.

With automated sync, Argo CD applies a new commit at the tracked revision without a manual sync, once it detects it; one commit to a path read by several Applications reaches all. prune: true lets automated sync delete live objects no longer in Git.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs v3.1: User Guide > Automated Sync Policy (Automatic Pruning); FAQ: how often does Argo CD check for changes

claims.text: applicationset.txt @ stage-4: echo-donhang-north/south point at their control-plane:6443, Synced Healthy, beside staging (kubernetes.default.svc); after one commit (greetings from -> hello from) both answer hello from <node>; then it deletes the ApplicationSet, both Secrets, platform/regions/.

echo-region.yaml @ stage-4: Caddy answers 'greetings from {env.NODE_NAME}', NODE_NAME from the downward API (spec.nodeName), in namespace regions, NodePort 30090; each region has one node, so the answer names the cluster.

The API server authenticates a caller by an X.509 client certificate (and its key) as kubectl presents from a kubeconfig; kind's kubeconfig holds the admin one (bound to cluster-admin), so a holder can change everything in that cluster.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Authenticating > X509 client certificates; kubeadm certificates (admin.conf, kubeadm:cluster-admins); kind Quick Start; applicationset.sh 45-46

claims.text: While the lab runs, donhang-north has a namespace regions, created by echo-region.yaml through its Application, and no namespace argocd, since regions-up.sh installs nothing in the regions; the context lives only in secrets/regions.kubeconfig.
Each Application has its own sync status and health status, so one Application generated by an ApplicationSet can be OutOfSync while another is Synced.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs v3.1: Core Concepts (sync status, health); ApplicationSet introduction

claims.text: Opinion: when every region shares path and revision, a commit (a mistake included) reaches all regions at their next sync; letting one region go first needs a path or revision per region in the template.

Opinion: Argo CD holding admin credentials for every registered cluster makes its blast radius, and that of config repository write access and read access to the cluster Secrets, cover all regions at once.

Opinion: with few clusters and none planned, hand-written Applications cost little; an ApplicationSet pays off when clusters are added or removed often, or when regions must stay alike by construction.
